subject: Kickoff: Evergreen Health dedicated capacity turn-up and ops schedule
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Evergreen Health dedicated capacity turn-up and ops schedule

Team —

Per our sales handoff, Evergreen Health (Raj Patel / ops-infra) signed for a small reserved GPU pool + burst. I want to align on the operational plan and surface any blockers before we commit dates. High-level ask from them: low-latency inference for clinical triage models, initial steady-state ~4 concurrent sessions, bursts up to 8 for peak hours. They prefer US-West region.

Please review the questions below and flag if you need more context: 
- Preferred instance type: customer noted "A100-equivalent" in call; we should confirm whether G5/RTX or A100-80GB variant is recommended.
- Initial pool sizing: propose 4 reserved GPUs with autoscale to +4 burst. Thoughts on safe burst policy (prewarm, cold-start risk)?
- Testing & validation window: need perf tests (p95 latency), load-plan owner and dates.
- Network/peering requirements and private IP constraints (customer will provide firewall rules).

I attached the preliminary runbook draft (evergreen-mop-v1.pdf) — please annotate changes inline. Plan to propose a go-live window of Apr 11–18 but that is flexible.

Jonas
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evergreen-mop-v1.pdf (runbook stub)
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@evergreenhealth.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-infra@evergreenhealth.ai, Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@evergreenhealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Evergreen Health dedicated capacity turn-up and ops schedule

Thanks Jonas — looping ops. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Hardware: we prefer A100-class for model consistency but can accept G5 if latency numbers match. Cost sensitivity is moderate — can mix reserved + burst at different families if needed.
- Region: US-West1 (closest to our EHR cluster).
- Workload profile: short-form inference (avg 120 tokens), spikes daily at 08:00–10:00 and 19:00–20:00 PST. Baseline QPS ~30, peak QPS ~150.
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress; we need a short network checklist for our security team.
- Procurement: SOW and DocuSign ready; procurement needs final SOW and pricing to execute within 2 weeks.

Attached: network-firewall-rules.xlsx (outbound/ingress summary).

Raj
Ops Lead, Evergreen Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 17 Mar 2028 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Evergreen Health dedicated capacity turn-up and ops schedule

Thanks Raj — appreciate the profile and the firewall sheet. I sketched a minimally invasive activation plan below (targets, owners, and blockers). Comments welcome.

Activation plan (proposed):
1) SOW sign & procurement (Sergio) — target: 2 business days after SOW finalization.
2) Network & peering validation (Raj + Redwood network lead) — target: parallel with SOW, need explicit firewall egress rules + IP allowlist.
3) Provision reserved pool: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs, dedicated network, prewarm images — (Redwood infra) target: 3 business days after net validation.
4) Load/perf validation: run 48h smoke & 8h soak with spike patterns (Marissa to own). Acceptance = p95 <= 220ms for p50 workload; no >5% error ratio.
5) Autoscale & burst policy: enable burst to +4 GPUs with a 30s startup buffer and a 10min cooldown. Prewarming: maintain a 1-GPU prewarm sentinel during predicted spikes. (Rationale: reduce cold-start cost while allowing elastic capacity).
6) Go/no-go checklist & runbooks delivered to customer support + SRE.

Risks/Notes:
- If we use heterogeneous hardware for burst (G5 vs A100), we may see quantization/latency variance — Marissa should run cross-variant perf tests.
- Network egress rules need confirmation for health-check endpoints (we will provide a short list).
- If procurement delays past Apr 1 we should shift the target window.

Attachments I will upload: evergreen-mop-v1.pdf (runbook), capacity-diagram.png (pool topology). I linked our internal activation page: https://redwood.example.com/s/evh-docs

Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference

- I will own the load test plan and execute the smoke/soak. Proposed windows: Apr 4 (smoke 2h) and Apr 6 (soak 8h) — target before SOW is fully executed so we can validate infra choices in staging.
